evidence: A calculation on committed products and published values: load Love numbers of a published lunar interior (Briaud et al. 2023's tidal fit: density and rigidity by layer, fluid core), elastic by integration of the static self-gravitating equations, relaxed as a thin elastic shell over an interior in hydrostatic equilibrium with the published effective elastic thicknesses of the mare basins; the sea-level equation with migrating shorelines solved on LOLA at 16 px/deg with spherical harmonics to degree 359. Checked against closed forms (homogeneous sphere, Boussinesq limit, fluid limit) and against the Moon's measured k2 and h2. Not validated against any observed loading on the Moon, which has none of this size.
reading_rule: Read 'elastic' as the response within years of the water's arrival and 'relaxed, Te' as the state the mantle's flow approaches over the relaxation times given (thousands to hundreds of thousands of years). 'volume' holds today's water (the atlas's 28% inventory) and lets the shore move; 'share' holds 28% cover and gives the water that takes. Sill depths are below the sea surface, four-connected cells at 16 px/deg. Sag is the ground's radial fall (degrees 2 and up, and degree 1 in the solid Moon's frame); 'relative' is the fall below the sea's equipotential. The products of geography are not regenerated: whether to move the shorelines is a decision this informs.
